title: Chronometer probes for per-subtoken timing and KV-hit chargeback
creator: Sana Patel
description: Add lightweight per-subtoken chronometer probes in the serving runtime to attribute latency and cost to individual subtokens and KV cache interactions. Motivation: current request-level and per-sequence metrics mask micro-latency sources (KV cache deserialization, kernel-switch overhead, per-layer token emission) that matter for accurate cost allocation and for automatic routing/caching policies. This ticket covers probe placement, span/metric naming, sampling strategy, downstream aggregation changes, and dashboarding for chargeback and regression detection.
implementation_notes: Instrument four probe points per emission: pre-kv-lookup, post-kv-hit, start-attention-step, end-token-emit. Each probe records monotonic nanoseconds and minimal metadata (model_variant, avx_level, request_origin, trace_id, token_index).

Use a per-thread ring buffer to append probe events and flush as part of the existing request-batched write to the telemetry pipeline to avoid extra RPCs. Buffer entry size target: <= 64 bytes to keep memory pressure low.

Aggregate probes into aggregated spans at 100ms or when request completes, emitting: token_latency_ns, kv_lookup_ns, kv_hit:boolean, kernel_switch_ns. Export via OTLP batcher to our metrics ingestion gateway with a new metrics schema version v2.
Sampling: default 1% uniformly across requests, 100% on flagged canary routes and internal test harnesses. Support adaptive sampling: increase sample rate when per-route 95th latency regresses > 15%.
Data retention: raw probe events retained for 7d in BigQuery for postmortems; aggregated rollups (per-model, per-route, per-hour) retained in TSDB for 90d.
Backwards compatibility: probes are guarded by runtime feature flag 'chronometer-probes'. When disabled there is zero additional metric emission and codepaths are elided.

Overhead estimates from local microbenchmarks: wall-clock additional latency per emission < 15us median when buffered; CPU usage +0.6% on sample workloads. End-to-end network overhead depends on sample rate; at 1% sample rate expected telemetry egress +1.3%.
Security: recorded token text must never be logged. Probes will include only token_index and token_hash truncated to 64 bits. No user PII will be included.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime emits chronometer spans when feature flag enabled and remains silent when disabled.
Aggregated per-token latency and kv_hit rates are visible in a new dashboard with per-model and per-route breakdowns.
PromQL and BigQuery queries compute per-token cost attribution within 5% of sampled ground truth for synthetic workloads.
Canary rollout exercised on dedicated pool without detectable SLA regressions (latency p50/p95 within 2% of baseline).
On-call playbook updated with queries to triage token-level regressions.
Design doc and PR reviewed by runtime and observability reviewers and merged.
observability_queries: PromQL: sum by(model_variant) (rate(token_latency_ns_sum[5m])) / sum by(model_variant) (rate(token_latency_ns_count[5m]))  # per-token avg latency
PromQL: sum by(route) (rate(kv_hit_total[5m])) / sum by(route) (rate(kv_lookup_total[5m]))  # kv cache hit rate by route

BigQuery: SELECT model_variant, route, token_index, AVG(token_latency_ns) as avg_ns FROM telemetry.chronometer_probe_events WHERE _PARTITIONTIME BETWEEN DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 7 DAY) AND CURRENT_DATE() GROUP BY model_variant, route, token_index ORDER BY avg_ns DESC LIMIT 100

Sample SQL for chargeback: SELECT route, SUM(CASE WHEN kv_hit THEN kv_lookup_ns ELSE token_latency_ns END) as reimbursable_ns FROM telemetry.chronometer_rollups WHERE ts BETWEEN TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 1 HOUR) AND CURRENT_TIMESTAMP() GROUP BY route
comments: 2025-02-20 Sana Patel: Triage notes — this unblocks several perf debugging stories and the billing team request for per-token chargeback. Prioritize minimal overhead and clear privacy controls.

2025-02-21 Marco Li: POC implemented in runtime branch feat/chronometer. Local microbenchmarks attached. Observed ~12us median extra per-emission when flushing buffer synchronously; switched to async batch flush to telemetry to reduce tail.

2025-02-23 Olivia Brooks (Observability): Reviewed schema v2. Asked for a deterministic span name pattern 'chronometer.token.v2.{probe_point}' and a compact tag set. Also requested we emit kv_hit as boolean metric and kv_lookup_ns separately for better aggregation.
2025-02-24 Marco Li: Addressed review comments, updated PR to use OTLP batcher and added adaptive sampling config. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2847
2025-02-25 QA: Ran canary on internal dedicated pool with 5k synthetic requests. No p95 regressions observed. Measurements show telemetry ingestion sustained; need to validate cost at 5% sample rate.
2025-02-26 Security (Kara Nguyen): Confirmed token content is not emitted. Recommended adding periodic audits to verify no accidental PII leakage in future schema changes.
2025-02-27 Marco Li: Moving to In Progress -> preparing canary rollout ticket and dashboard panels. Will split rollout and cost-analysis into follow-up tickets.
risk_mitigation: Guard all probe code behind feature flag to allow instant rollback.
Use sampling and per-thread buffers to keep overhead bounded; default to low sample rate (1%).
Dashboard will include probe-emission-rate and telemetry-ingest-error panels; automation will disable probes if telemetry error rate exceeds threshold.
Cost analysis follow-up ticket to confirm telemetry egress does not exceed budget at higher sample rates.
